catalog.name: ghsl-historical-pr-v2
catalog.label_provenance: Targets from Security Lab reports. Commit pairs are real upstream history, mined and refuted by separate AI agents reading source. No human review and no exploit execution.
limitations: Labels rest on source reading by AI agents; nothing was executed and no human reviewed them.
Clean-control claims cover only the shown diff, not the tree.
Controls are real commits but were selected near dangerous code, so their mix does not represent ordinary PR traffic.
Several entries are reversed fixes, whose diffs read as removals rather than new code.
Only targets with a clean introducing commit or reverted fix are used; the suite deliberately does not cover all 49 catalog targets.
Cases within a repository are correlated, and several targets can share one PR, so they are not independent trials.

labels.title: JSON injection
labels.mechanism: Username, email, password and similar values from /logIn, /signUp and reset requests reach AuthServiceClient, which builds backend JSON with String.format and no escaping. Quotes in those values inject extra keys such as userId or userUrn that shadow the trusted fields.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
Frontend string-formatted JSON incorporates attacker-controlled values, allowing injected fields to shadow trusted fields.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: Fallback: the introductions are f49666a (USER_ID_FIELD, 204 files) and fdf4e484 (signUp/verify/reset bodies, 49 non-generated files, +2539/-47), both oversized. Backend last-key-wins parsing is from the advisory, not verified here. The diff also carries an AuthenticationController refactor (Http.Request parameters, withSession) and routes changes. The base-side session change has a functional bug fixed later by 011421df; it is not part of this target.

labels.title: Path traversal
labels.mechanism: Any signed-in user GETs admin/media/download_private_file?file=... AdminController only applies cama_authenticate and the action has no authorize!. params[:file] goes to CamaleonCmsLocalUploader.private_file_path, which runs Rails.root.join('private', site_id, key) with only repeated slashes collapsed. ../ sequences, or an absolute path by Pathname#join semantics, leave the private root; if the file exists it is passed to send_file.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
An ordinary authenticated user's file parameter reaches send_file through download_private_file without enforcing the private-media root.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: The mechanism differs from the 2.8.0 code in the advisory: head uses private_file_path and File.exist?. The fetch_file("private/#{params[:file]}") form dates from the refactor in 9931e11357a1f4b83256367b2d75ac9679b59f7d. The controller-to-send_file flow and the missing root check are the same. Traversal depth also differs because the root here is <Rails.root>/private/<site id>. The commit bundles unrelated work (private custom fields, uploader cache keys, JS). It also adds a hidden label_eval form field; that is not credited here because the eval sink is already at base and GHSL-2024-185 belongs to 020eebc3. Not executed; the path semantics come from reading the code.

also_valid.description: New private media mode has no authorization: any signed-in user can pass private=1 to media#ajax (list private files, no authorize! on ajax) and media#upload (write into the private tree). Private files are also downloadable by any signed-in user, with no ownership or role check.
also_valid.evidence: app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/media_controller.rb:89 at 9e49d37e (init_media_vars), and the ajax and upload actions at the same commit

cases.caveats: Different file from the catalog targets; same path-injection class. Incomplete: chatId stays unchecked in streamStorageFile until c00ae78488a802beb82ee095c82910e0cb539ef4 (#5208). _sanitizeFilename can return an empty string, in which case path.join resolves to the directory itself; that is an edge case and not assessed further. Counts exclude lockfile changes.
Sits in the same chain as 079, generalizing the earlier fix to other hop headers.
Withheld pending private disclosure; see .bench/private/pr-v2-review.

GHSL-2025-012, 013, and 014 sinks remain at head in the called functions, so this is not a fix. Quoting in the removed copies and in the called functions was not compared argument by argument; that is why confidence is medium. Ten i18n lines are also added.

labels.title: Path traversal / file read
labels.mechanism: Authenticated user supplies GET download_file?file_name=../.. ; params[:file_name] is joined to ASSIGNMENTS_DIR/<short_identifier> with File.join, checked only with File.exists?, then passed to send_file. No containment check at head.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
An attacker-controlled path in AutomatedTestsController#download_file reaches a file download without effective containment, enabling unintended file reads under the documented account permissions.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: Mismatch with catalog: the advisory (v2.4.6) describes instructors and assignment.autotest_files_dir. At this commit the join uses ASSIGNMENTS_DIR/short_identifier, and download_file is outside the authorize_only_for_admin list, with only the global authenticate before_action seen, so reach looks wider (any authenticated user; a code reading, not run). Later edits 057b4e0a and d9cb2555 only changed the base directory. The same diff also adds upload_files with File.join(autotest_path, f) before File.delete, and with f.original_filename before File.write; those are related but not credited here. The existing `download` action makes the traversal pattern pre-existing in this controller.

also_valid.description: Arbitrary file deletion: upload_files is new, has no admin guard, and passes params[:delete_files] entries through File.join to File.delete.
also_valid.evidence: app/controllers/automated_tests_controller.rb upload_files, delete_files loop, at f85c6261; route post 'upload_files' at config/routes.rb

also_valid.description: Broken access control: the diff removes fetch_testers and populate_file_manager from authorize_only_for_admin, so any authenticated user can enqueue AutotestTestersJob and list autotest files.

cases.caveats: The 500 branch includes error text in the response, but that text holds no request data. Version disclosure is minor and the route is not whitelisted from basic auth. PR link derived from the first merge subject on the ancestry path.
The same script tag holds a pre-existing raw(params[:field_options]...) expression; the diff does not change that part.

Touches the file and helper behind GHSL-2024-066. base_bath is a functional bug in dead code. The later commit e499f481 removes that early return, which is why it was rejected as a control (see selection_notes). The create path gains the course name, matching base_path.

labels.title: Reflected XSS
labels.mechanism: A crafted URL controls req.params.id on GET /api/v1/public-chatflows/:id -> findOneBy returns nothing for an unknown id -> res.status(404).send() interpolates the id unencoded -> Express sends a string body as text/html by default, so markup in the id renders in the victim browser. The route is whitelisted from basic auth in the same diff.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.

The /api/v1/public-chatflows/:id endpoint reflects an attacker-controlled identifier into an HTML error response without encoding, allowing script execution under the report's configuration assumptions.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: The same reflection already exists at base in sibling routes such as GET /api/v1/chatflows/:id (head line 186), so this adds a new instance of an existing pattern. A reviewer flagging only those older lines has not identified this diff. text/html comes from Express default behaviour, not from code in this repo, and was not run. A non-UUID id is assumed to return null on the default SQLite; a stricter database may raise an error instead (not tested). The isPublic check applies only when a chatflow is found, so it does not guard the 404 path.

also_valid.description: Public, basic-auth-exempt endpoint returns the whole chatflow row including flowData for isPublic flows; at this commit node API keys are stored in flowData inputs, so sharing a chatbot publicly discloses them.
also_valid.evidence: packages/server/src/index.ts:194 at 7141401e (res.json(chatflow)); packages/components/nodes/llms/OpenAI/OpenAI.ts:123 at 7141401e reads openAIApiKey from nodeData.inputs

cases.caveats: Sits beside a pre-existing reflected name in a thrown Error, which this diff does not change. Small, but a real logic change adjacent to the sanitizer.

labels.title: Code injection
labels.mechanism: Precondition: an administrator, or anyone holding the settings permission (authorize! :manager, :settings), or an account takeover of one. CustomFieldsController passes params[:fields] and params[:field_options] to add_fields, which stores the options hash verbatim with set_meta('_default', options), so a crafted field_options[..][label_eval]=true is kept; field name and description are mass-assignable. When a form renders the field, _render.html.erb calls eval(@field.name) and eval(@field.description), running the text as Ruby on the server.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
An administrator can enable label_eval and supply custom field text evaluated as Ruby; the report chains this with account takeover, so administrator prerequisites must be stated.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: At head no form control sets label_eval, so enabling it needs a crafted POST or programmatic add_field. _get_items gains a hidden field that round-trips the option only in 9e49d37e, and the advisory's PoC is also a crafted POST. The sink and the persistence are both in place at head. Administrator prerequisite must be stated; the advisory chains this with account takeover. The commit is a grab bag of 18 files with one line of documentation and two view lines for this feature, so the signal is small. Not executed. Correction from review: at base the name could already be evaluated when it starts with t(, so this is a distinct new sink behind options[:label_eval], not the first administrator route to eval.

labels.mechanism: Caller of POST upload_files supplies params[:path]; it is joined with assignment.autotest_files_dir and f.original_filename with File.join and written by File.write with no containment check.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.

Untrusted path data from AutomatedTestsController reaches filesystem writes outside the intended repository directory; arbitrary Ruby writes can lead to delayed code execution under the documented permissions.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: Partial introduction: the File.write sink and the f.original_filename join already exist at base (added in f85c6261 with autotest_path). This commit adds only the params[:path] vector that the advisory PoC uses. The advisory also calls original_filename untrusted; I did not verify whether it could carry traversal at base (depends on Rack filename handling), so base may not be fully clean for this sink. FileUtils.mkdir_p was added later (91f49f99) and zip handling later (728bb9cb), so the zip-entry vector post-dates head. Mismatch with catalog: upload_files is outside the admin list at this commit, so reach looks wider than instructors (code reading, not run). The diff also adds new_folders/delete_folders joins (mkdir_p, rm_rf) on untrusted names, which a reviewer may reasonably also flag.

Arbitrary recursive deletion: params[:delete_folders] entries are joined and passed to FileUtils.rm_rf with no containment.

labels.title: Arbitrary file deletion
labels.mechanism: Requires authorize! :manage, :media, so an administrator or media manager, or an account takeover of one; this is not unauthenticated. MediaController#actions with media_action=del_file or del_folder passes params[:folder] (only // collapsed) to CamaleonCmsLocalUploader#delete_file / #delete_folder, which run FileUtils.rm or FileUtils.rm_rf on File.join(@root_folder, key) with no containment.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
An administrator-controlled folder parameter reaches the local uploader deletion operation without containment; do not describe this as an unauthenticated deletion.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: fix_reverted: head is the parent of base by design. Why no introduction is used: del_file first appears in a1c4ee4d971d715d95694604d783d9e4227558d9, but that commit hard-codes an AWS test connection, so the local backend is not active there; its param is params[:file] and it deletes through the external Fog gem. b81a85a7086b1599544a614b9090eec66e8e3653 turns on the local default but does not touch the del_file code; 7b1dce32637dd3dc029218577a3fae9aa4259de2 only renames the param to params[:folder]; 4043ca1f81535a648ae2ef7fe8e44b2658f5b657 only swaps the backend. No single commit introduces the catalog mechanism. The a1c4ee4d and b81a85a7 diffs also contain a hard-coded AWS key pair from upstream history, which is another reason to keep them out of a benchmark. This diff also reverts the error-rendering refactor and restores @args[:root_folder], which is not attacker-settable. Upstream later hardened delete_folder further (ff19dde4, 2026-08-31), so base is not fully contained. add_folder and the crop_url action mentioned by the advisory are unchanged here.

labels.title: System account impersonation
labels.mechanism: An authenticated user sends X-DATAHUB-ACTOR (different case). The proxy's case-sensitive filter does not remove it, so it is forwarded to GMS, where NoOpAuthenticator looks up the actor header in a case-insensitive map and takes that identity for authorization.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
In the default unauthenticated metadata-service configuration, NoOpAuthenticator trusts the caller's X-DataHub-Actor header for authorization identity.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: Fallback: the introduction f49666a is 204 files, +3966/-1193, unusable. 079: confidence medium. The catalog names NoOpAuthenticator, but its code is unchanged across this pair and direct GMS access still trusts the header at base; the diff only covers the frontend filter bypass the advisory demonstrates. 083: confidence low, credited only partly. The diff removes the browser-side session reset, but server-side invalidation exists on neither side, so replay of a retained cookie works at base too. The catalog wording ('clears the browser cookie') describes base here, not head; the advisory says cookies are not cleared on logout, which matches head. bc2e71e9 (#3049, first server logout route) was rejected as an introduction because base already had client-only logout and the same cookie acceptance. SCORING WARNING: this head also reintroduces 076 (mapPath slash guard) and 081 (catch-all in AuthenticationManager). They are credited to their own introduced_historical entries, so a reviewer reporting them here is correct and must not be scored a false positive.

also_valid.description: Head removes the leading-slash guard in mapPath, re-enabling destination host change via /api/gms@host.
Head restores the empty catch (Exception), so a JAAS misconfiguration authenticates arbitrary credentials; tryLogin sets loginSucceeded after a normal return.
GHSL-2022-083 is not scored here, but a correct finding about it is valid for this diff.
also_valid.evidence: See the target definition in the snapshot catalog.

cases.caveats: GHSL-2025-021 exists at base in the edited function and is neither fixed nor worsened. Trimming is not sanitization.

labels.title: Insecure secret encryption
labels.mechanism: Stored DataHub secrets are encrypted by SecretService with Cipher.getInstance("AES") and a SHA-1-derived key. Under the default JCE provider that transformation resolves to AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding, so identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks to anyone who can read the stored values. This reveals repeated structure, not plaintext or the key.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
SecretUtils and SecretService encrypt secrets with AES ECB, revealing repeated-block structure; explain the confidentiality consequence rather than claiming arbitrary decryption.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: Partial for the catalog target. Fallback: the introduction 271784c9 is 148 non-generated files, +8224/-344, unusable. Head does not literally say ECB because 2c9e3b74 had rewritten the string to "AES"; a reviewer must know the provider default, which comes from JCE behaviour rather than this repo. SecretService moved from metadata-io to metadata-operation-context after v0.8.44. SecretUtils is ECB at base and head, and legacy decrypt stays at base. 341 of the changed lines are a test file. Not in v0.8.45: the fix is from 2025-07-02.

also_valid.description: Head removes authenticated encryption, so stored ciphertext has no integrity protection and blocks can be altered or rearranged undetected.
Head derives a 128-bit key from truncated SHA-1 for new encryptions, replacing the HMAC-SHA256 derived 256-bit key.
also_valid.evidence: SecretService.java:46 at fa7b4132 versus deriveKey in the diff at 9b26c8d5

labels.title: Authentication fails open
labels.mechanism: During JAAS login, a non-LoginException raised while building the LoginContext (for example from a malformed jaas.conf) is swallowed by a new empty catch (Exception). authenticateUser returns normally, so the caller treats any username and password as authenticated and issues a session token.
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
An erroneous JAAS configuration causes authentication to accept arbitrary credentials rather than rejecting login.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: Commit is titled as a dependency bump; the security-relevant change is an incidental catch-all. The exception path comes from code reading plus the advisory (it reports an IOException from a malformed jaas.conf); not executed. The method was later renamed authenticateJaasUser. Head of fix-reverted-frontend-minor-issues also reintroduces this flaw; 081 is credited here only.

labels.title: Untrusted deserialization
labels.mechanism: With SSO enabled, a user with an account at the IdP can place a {#sb64}-prefixed serialized object in the nonce or another id_token claim. pac4j 3.6.0 deserializes it in InternalAttributeHandler.restore during the OIDC callback.
labels.location_hint: pac4j nonce handling and dependency version
evidence_required: Identify the attacker-controlled input or capability and relevant preconditions.
Trace that input to the affected operation using concrete repository locations.
Explain the absent or ineffective defense and the resulting security consequence.
The affected pac4j dependency deserializes attacker-controlled nonce data, creating the reported untrusted deserialization path.
Explain why the proposed diff introduces the issue relative to base.

cases.caveats: The sink is in the dependency, not this repo, so the flow past the callback could not be read from code at this commit; it comes from the advisory and GHSA-76mw-6p95-x9x5. Exploit impact needs a usable gadget chain within RestrictedObjectInputStream. Fallback: the introduction 08616cc6 is 42 non-generated files, +1013/-245, over both limits. The signal is one version line inside a 660-line Play framework migration with many unrelated changes. Not in v0.8.45 or v0.9.0, both of which still pin 3.6.0; v0.9.6 is the first checked tag with 4.5.7.

A finding naming a real known vulnerability in one of these downgraded versions should not count as a false positive; specific CVEs were not verified here.

labels.mechanism: A logged-in client requests /api/gms@host/... ; the /api/*path route reaches Application.proxy; mapPath strips the /api/gms prefix with no leading-slash guarantee, and the remainder is concatenated straight after the port in http://%s:%s%s, so userinfo syntax moves the destination host to the attacker's choice. The XSS interpretation follows from relaying the body and content type, read from code; nothing was run, and '@' handling by the WS client is taken from the advisory. Head of fix-reverted-frontend-minor-issues also reintroduces this flaw; 076 is credited here only.
